name: com.gitbook/mcp
title: GitBook
description: Full read/write access to a GitBook organization: build sites and spaces, edit content, publish.

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: Lists the published sites in a GitBook organization, the usual entry point for orientation. Returns each site's title, visibility, hostname and id. To reach site content, use this first to find a site, then get_site_structure to see the spaces (where content lives) within it. Not for listing a site's content directly (use get_site_structure).

tools.name: get_site_structure
tools.description: Returns a site's navigation structure: its sections, groups, external links (with destination URLs), and published spaces, with the paths and ids needed to read content. Pass the organization id (the same one used with list_sites) and the site id. Use it to map a site before reading or editing. Find a site first with list_sites; read page content with get_page.

tools.name: list_site_topics
tools.description: Lists the topics and subtopics a site's content and visitor questions are organised under, ranked by how many Ask AI questions they drew over the range, with each one's answered rate, open findings and id. Use it to find which topics visitors ask about most or struggle with, to resolve a topic by name, or to discover a topic id before filtering Ask AI questions, answers or stats by topic (the `topic` parameter of getSiteQuestionStats, listSiteQuestions and listSiteQuestionAnswers). Use getSiteTopicById for a single topic's summary.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Returns a page's content as markdown plus its id, title and path. Look the page up by pageId or by path. Use it to read content before editing. Find a space with get_site_structure; to list that space's pages, use the operation surface — invoke_operation getSpaceById to read its `revision`, then getRevisionById to get the revision's pages.

tools.name: create_change_request
tools.description: Opens a change request on a space. Published content is never edited directly: create a change request, edit pages within it, then submit/merge it. Returns the new change request id needed for those follow-ups. When the change request fixes a documentation issue found by GitBook, pass siteFindingId so merging it resolves the finding. See get_usage_guide("editing").

tools.name: submit_or_merge_change_request
tools.description: Merges a change request, publishing its edits to the space. This is destructive and irreversible. Use it to finish the editing flow after create_change_request and editing pages via updateChangeRequestContent. Reports conflicts instead of merging when the change request is out of date.

tools.name: get_subscription_information
tools.description: Returns a GitBook organization's subscription: whether it is on a trial, the free plan or a paid plan, when an active trial ends and how many days are left, and where to upgrade. Use it to answer questions such as "What plan am I on?", "How long is left on my trial?" or "How do I upgrade?", and before relying on features that need a paid site plan (sections, advanced customization, custom domains). Give the user upgradeUrl only when canManageBilling is true; otherwise, tell them an administrator of the organization has to upgrade, and share pricingUrl to compare plans.

tools.name: get_usage_guide
tools.description: Returns procedural guidance for working with GitBook through this server (content model and step-by-step recipes). Call it when unsure how to orient, read, or edit content. Omit topic to list available topics.

tools.name: report_tool_feedback
tools.description: Reports a problem you hit while using this server's tools or operations, or an improvement worth making, so they can be fixed. Use it the moment you run into friction: a confusing tool or parameter, a call that failed or returned something unusable, a task that took far more calls than it should have, or something you needed that no tool or operation could do. It also takes suggestions when nothing went wrong; there is no category for those yet, so pick the one the improvement is about. Report the tool or operation itself, not the content it returned. Reporting is cheap and does not affect your current task, so prefer reporting over staying silent; then carry on with what you were doing.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Searches the GitBook API operations this server can run, returning matches (id, method, path, summary) to run with invoke_operation. Use describe_operation for an operation's inputs. Use it to find operations beyond the curated tools. Read-only.

tools.name: describe_operation
tools.description: Describes one GitBook API operation found via search: its path/query parameters and request-body JSON Schema, so you can build params for invoke_operation. Read-only.

tools.name: invoke_operation
tools.description: Runs one GitBook API operation discovered via search, for capabilities not covered by a curated tool. Pass operationId and params (path/query/body). Returns the operation's JSON response, or a one-line status when the operation answers with no content. The surface includes operations that are visible to the public or cannot be undone (for example publishing a site or merging a change request), so confirm before invoking one.
